title: Performance & Benchmarking Sync - 2026-03-03
content:
Meeting: Performance & Benchmarking sync (standup-style)
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 09:00 PT (30m)
Attendees: Asha Patel, Miguel Lopez, Samantha Chen, Rajiv Menon, Evelyn Wu

Goal:
- Triage the latency/throughput regressions observed in the hosted API (production and dedicated) since 2026-02-28.
- Agree on repro steps, short-term mitigations, and owner assignments for fixes/testing.

Summary of issue:
- Starting 2026-02-28 evening deploy, p95/p99 token latency increased for long-sequence (>=1024) generation workloads on the redwood-13B-v2 model family on A100 clusters.
- Overall throughput (tokens/s per GPU) dropped ~18% at 1024 seq, ~25% at 2048 seq, compared to the 2026-02-26 baseline.
- Short-sequence workloads (<=128) show no measurable regression (<3% variation).
- Regression reproducible in perf-harness synthetic tests and in a subset of customer requests that exercise long continuations.

Key observations / data points:
- Baseline (2026-02-26 commit abc9f4): A100 80GB, FP16, batch 1, seq=1024: p50=120ms, p95=190ms, p99=260ms, tokens/s/GPU=21000.
- Current (2026-03-02 after deploy commit 1b7c33): A100 80GB, FP16, batch 1, seq=1024: p50=140ms, p95=225ms, p99=325ms, tokens/s/GPU=17000.
- H100 runs show smaller regression (~8-12%) but still present.
- Quantized INT8 (experimental path) shows similar relative degradation vs its baseline.
- Kernel-selection trace (perf-harness --trace-kernels) shows different attention kernel chosen for some layer shapes on the new runtime binary.
- CUDA driver differences: nodes running driver 535.x show worse regression than 534.x; however driver rollout overlaps with runtime deploy making causality unclear.

Repro steps (quick):
- Checkout serving-runtime @ commit 1b7c33 and abc9f4 locally to compare.
- Run: python perf-harness/bench.py --model redwood-13B-v2 --device a100 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --profile --repeat 10
- Capture kernel trace: python perf-harness/bench.py --model redwood-13B-v2 --device a100 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --trace-kernels --out /tmp/kernels_new.json
- Repeat on a node with driver 534.x and 535.x (we have both in staging pools).

Hypotheses discussed:
1) Kernel selector regression introduced in PR #4567 (serving-runtime) that changes heuristic for attention kernel selection on long sequences; causes less-optimal kernels to be used for some layer shapes.
2) CUDA driver 535.x interacts with our new fused attention path and causes higher runtime for large sequence kernels.
3) Memory allocator path changes (recent arena tweak) increase fragmentation leading to extra synchronization and worse batching efficiency at high-seq lengths.

Evidence so far:
- Kernel traces differ between abc9f4 and 1b7c33 on same hardware. The new traces show more calls to a slower generic attention kernel at seq=1024 for layer shapes (seq, head=64, head_dim=64) in certain layers.
- Reverting only PR #4567 locally returns kernel selection to baseline and restores ~90% of throughput in perf harness runs.
- Staging nodes on driver 534.x + runtime 1b7c33 are ~6% faster than 535.x + runtime 1b7c33, but still slower than full baseline, so driver alone is not the whole story.

Short-term mitigations (agreed):
- Roll back PR #4567 from the hosted A100 fleet for missions-critical routes until root cause is fixed (owner: Miguel). Target: rollback window today 15:00 PT.
- Add explicit kernel-override flag in perf-harness/runtime to force baseline kernel selector for long-seq tests while we iterate (owner: Samantha).
- Pin CUDA driver to 534.x in dedicated/staging pools while we validate (owner: Rajiv + infra request ticket).

Action items and owners:
- Miguel Lopez: Prepare and execute rollback of PR #4567 to hosted A100 cluster for affected routes. Coordinate with deployments channel and SRE. ETA: 2026-03-03 15:00 PT.
- Samantha Chen: Add --kernel-selector-override to perf-harness and run an A/B perf suite across commits abc9f4 and 1b7c33 (seq 128/512/1024/2048). Post results to the ticket. ETA: 2026-03-04 EOD.
- Rajiv Menon: Open infra change request to pin driver 534.x for selected staging/dedicated pools. Provide list of nodes. ETA: 2026-03-03 EOD.
- Evelyn Wu: Gather customer impact data: list of affected customers & routes (from logs), percentage of requests >1024 seq. Prepare a short customer-facing note if rollback proceeds. ETA: 2026-03-03 12:00 PT.
- Asha Patel: Reproduce locally, capture kernel traces for both commits, attach to PR #4567 for the reviewer. Start a bisect if needed. ETA: 2026-03-04 11:00 PT.

Open questions / risks:
- If kernel-selector heuristic is the cause, do we take the simple path of reverting or implement a targeted selector-fix? Revert is faster but blocks selector improvements.
- Pinning drivers could delay other infra upgrades and security patches; need rollout plan to re-upgrade once fix in runtime.
- Regression also observed on H100 (albeit smaller) — ensures fix must be cross-vendor-architecture.

Data attachments / where to look:
- perf-harness results (raw CSVs) in ci artifacts: ci.perf.redwood/internal/perf-run-2026-03-03.
- Kernel traces attached to PR: /github/pr/4567/kernels/trace_new.json (linked in PR).
- Dashboard: Console -> Models -> redwood-13B-v2 -> Per-route latency (filter seq>=1024).

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick standup tomorrow 2026-03-04 09:00 PT to confirm rollback status and initial perf after rollback.
- Full postmortem draft if rollback deployed in prod. Owner for postmortem: Asha.

Notes to self / scribbles from meeting:
- Observed odd pattern where layer 6/12 and 9/12 choose generic kernel; maybe due to odd head_dim rounding.
- Check kernel selector code path around attention tile-size heuristics.
- Consider adding microbenchmarks for individual attention shapes to CI.

Meeting closed at 09:30 PT.

This document is a working note — will be updated as we get traces, rollback confirmation, and perf runs.
